target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits to requestTimeoutMs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over websocket/unix transport would hang forever on initialize/RPC when a peer accepted the socket but never completed the WebSocket upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Bound upgrades with `ws.handshakeTimeout` **and** an explicit CONNECTING deadline. `ws.handshakeTimeout` alone does **not** abort custom `createConnection` (Unix) upgrades — verified with a never-upgrade unix peer that stayed CONNECTING past the library timeout.
- Production budget is resolved `appServer.requestTimeoutMs` (default 60s) from `CodexAppServerClient.start` via `resolveCodexAppServerRuntimeOptions()` — not a competing fixed 30s policy.
- Short `handshakeTimeoutMs` overrides remain test/proof-only hang floors.
- Restores `openApnsTlsTunnel` in the raw-socket CodeQL owner allowlist. Editing `transport-websocket.ts` path-triggers network Critical Quality, which evaluates the full tree and currently fails closed on that managed APNs proxy-TLS callsite (siblings `openProxiedApnsHttp2Session` / `connectApnsHttp2Session` are already classified on main). This is classification of an existing owner, not a Codex policy change.

Collision check: no competing open PR for the same hang.

## User Impact

- **Before:** never-upgrade peers hang initialize/RPC forever (TCP and Unix).
- **After:** handshake follows operator `requestTimeoutMs` (default 60s) on both TCP and Unix, then emits transport exit (`1006`).

## Evidence

Exact head: `29daa4fa3f6cef869efe41d9a864e8234fb902f1`

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run
```

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Coverage includes:
- reuses resolved `requestTimeoutMs` for websocket/unix handshake budgets
- negative control: plain `ws` without timeout stays CONNECTING
- TCP non-default budget (250ms) times out
- **Unix non-default budget (250ms) times out** (requires explicit CONNECTING deadline)
- initialize fails closed when handshake never completes

```bash
node --import tsx proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts
```

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=29daa4fa3f6cef869efe41d9a864e8234fb902f1
[case 1] negative control — ws without handshakeTimeout stays CONNECTING
  ok: without handshakeTimeout, stays CONNECTING after 300ms
[case 2] positive control — createWebSocketTransport times out
  ok: production handshake timeout matches requestTimeoutMs default (60s)
  info: killed=true exit_code=1006 elapsed_ms≈200 proof_timeout_ms=200 production_timeout_ms=60000
[case 3] valid server — client communicates over real WebSocket
  ok: RPC responded with expected result
=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

Current-`main` negative: Unix `createConnection` peer with only `ws.handshakeTimeout=300` stays CONNECTING past 2s (library timeout ignored). After fix: same peer exits via transport `exit` within the configured budget.

## Verification

- Exact head: `29daa4fa3f6cef869efe41d9a864e8234fb902f1`
- Rebased onto latest `origin/main`
- `oxfmt --check` on touched transport files — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- Focused tests: 8/8 passed
- Proof: 9/9 passed

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: stalled WebSocket upgrade hang on Codex app-server TCP/Unix transports.
Real env: Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0, production `createWebSocketTransport` + loopback peers.
What was not tested: live remote Codex app-server process / authenticated cloud endpoint.

## Risk / Compatibility

- Handshake reuses existing `requestTimeoutMs` (default 60s); operators with higher budgets keep that budget.
- CodeQL allowlist restore is required for path-triggered network Critical Quality; it classifies the existing managed APNs owner already adjacent to allowlisted siblings.
